cases.reason: GR6 governs the transfer INTO identifier-2 by the MOVE rules. In 2002 identifier-2 may be an implicit CD data-name, whose description comes only from Annex A. MESSAGE DATE is an unsigned 6-digit integer and STATUS KEY is a 2-character alphanumeric item, and both pass SR3. Items of a record under a CD also qualify (A.1.1.2). The receiver's description drives the MOVE, and the 2023 row (no communication section) cannot witness that case. This is the reach the reader itself used to call 14.1.3 GR8 DIFFERENT. The p-04 upholds of GR9 and GR10 do not apply, because those rules describe only the sender. Probe at --std 2002 (correct): ACCEPT IN-MDATE FROM DATE equals ACCEPT YMD FROM DATE, and ACCEPT IN-STATUS FROM DAY-OF-WEEK gives '7 ' (alphanumeric MOVE, left-justified). needs: a 2002 witness for implicit-CD-name and CD-record receivers. compiler-at-2002: correct.

cases.reason: A keyword-equivalence rule. It names no operand, list or deferral. ROUNDED becoming rounded-phrase does not touch it. The reader's 2002 probe of ADD CORR stands.

The rule's condition reads the USAGE of every operand ('none of the operands is described with usage binary-char ...'). In 2002 an operand of ADD may be an implicit CD data-name, and only Annex A gives its description: TEXT LENGTH is an unsigned 4-digit integer and MESSAGE COUNT an unsigned 6-digit integer, both numeric, so SR2 admits them. The 2023 row cannot witness how the rule applies to them. This is the same reach that p-14 and p-18 overturned for the arithmetic statements' category rules. Probe at --std 2002 (correct): ADD IN-LEN IN-COUNT TO W gives 133555; ADD 0.25 IN-LEN GIVING R gives 9999.25; ADD 1 TO IN-LEN (9999) raises SIZE ERROR and leaves 9999. needs: a 2002 witness for CD-item operands. compiler-at-2002: correct.

cases.reason: SR4 tests whether data-name-2 is a restricted data-pointer. In 2002 data-name-2 may be a level-01 pointer record under an output CD: A.1.2.2 SR9 puts no restriction on output-CD records, and USAGE SR13 asks only for level 1. The reader of p-16 already ruled this reach DIFFERENT for SR3 of this clause. A restricted pointer there (01 CP TYPE PT, with PT a TYPEDEF of USAGE POINTER TO T) is a 2002 case that the 2023 row cannot show. Probe at --std 2002: the working-storage form works (WP SET), but the CD record is refused at its declaration with COBOL0899 ('a shared record area of that shape is recognized but not yet implemented'). That is the defect p-16 already reported (cdptr.cob), so it is not new. needs: its own verdict; at --std 2002 the CD case is refused COBOL0899. compiler-at-2002: wrong (known p-16 defect).

The text is the same, and the 2023 changes (OPTIONS INITIALIZE) are confined to GR8 and GR9, which cover the case without INITIALIZED. The rule writes the allocated storage, not data-name-2, so the CD reach does not touch it.

This is a pure classification: identifier-4 and the identifiers in an expression are sending operands. It reads no property of the operand's description, so a CD-item identifier-4 is classified the same way. The reader's 2002 probe (IN-LEN passed BY VALUE, unchanged) stands. This matches the p-17 uphold of SR17. Format 3 of 2002 is format 2 of 2023, phrase for phrase.
It pairs a BY VALUE argument with a BY VALUE formal parameter. It reads nothing of the argument's description, and the program-prototype format is the same in both editions.

SR19 is a class test on identifier-4. In 2002 identifier-4 has no section limit and may be an implicit CD data-name whose class comes only from Annex A: TEXT LENGTH is numeric (legal BY VALUE), STATUS KEY is alphanumeric (illegal). This is the same reach that p-14 and p-18 overturned for class and category tests. The reader probed only the legal IN-LEN case and a working-storage negative. Probe at --std 2002 (correct): CALL 'S2' AS NESTED USING BY VALUE IN-STATUS is refused with COBOL1628 and COBOL1688. The message cites §2023:14.9.4.3 SR22; it should cite §2002:14.8.4.2 SR19 at --std 2002, a citation nit only. needs: a 2002 witness for implicit CD data-names as identifier-4. compiler-at-2002: correct.
